original_value: Infrared small target detection in a complex background has always been a challenging task in an infrared detection system. The existing methods based on the infrared patch image (IPI) model have achieved a good result but are sensitive to the complex background. So, to effectively detect the small target in complex background, model based on the reweighted IPI model along with total variance (TV) is proposed in this study. In this study firstly, the problem of using nuclear norm minimisation (NNM) in the existing IPI‐based methods is discussed, and a solution is proposed by replacing the existing NNM with the ℒp‐norm minimisation of singular values in the existing IPI methods. Secondly, a TV regularisation term is added to the background patch image to suppress the noise and preserve the strong edges in the background. The proposed method is solved by the alternating direction method of the multiplier. The robustness of the proposed method is validated by experimenting with the large dataset of real infrared images as well as the synthetic images. The proposed method not only has good background suppression ability, but also enhances and detect the target well in comparisons with the other baseline methods.

result.paraphrase: Infrared small-target detection against complex backgrounds has long been a difficult problem in infrared detection systems. Although infrared patch image (IPI)-based methods have produced good results, they remain sensitive to cluttered backgrounds. To improve small-target detection in complex scenes, this study proposes a reweighted IPI model combined with total variation (TV). First, it examines the use of nuclear norm minimization (NNM) in existing IPI-based methods and replaces it with ℒp-norm minimization of singular values within the IPI framework. Second, a TV regularization term is introduced into the background patch image to suppress noise while preserving strong background edges. The proposed method is solved using the alternating direction method of the multiplier. Its robustness is verified through experiments on a large dataset of real infrared images and synthetic images. Compared with other baseline methods, the proposed approach not only suppresses background effectively but also enhances and detects the target well.
